transcript.text: Hi everyone, I'm Mara, the Line Producer for the City Arts Gala. Before we get into the details, I want to make sure we run through the normal pre-lock round-robin so each of you can report your final operating requirements. Once I hear from technical, rights, talent, and accessibility leads, I'll make the binding production approval. Who'd like to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I'd like to start with technical. My radio-frequency survey is complete and there's a critical finding: wireless roaming camera links interfere with the theater's assistive-listening loop. Because of that, the gala must use three fixed wired cameras from the marked camera platforms. I filed the survey in the technical folder, but I want to make sure it's noted here that it's not on Mara's draft lock sheet yet.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to report on rights. I received the countersigned performance license this morning, and there's a critical restriction: the license permits the gala broadcast but prohibits any video-on-demand release or later promotional clips. The recording must be marked broadcast-only. I have not yet entered this restriction in the rights tracker, but I'm flagging it now during the round-robin. This means the current draft package's provision permitting the recording to be reused in the festival archive would violate the license terms.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to report on talent. I confirmed with the headliner's agent that the performer can soundcheck only at exactly 3:00 PM on Saturday, and the rider prohibits sponsor product placement anywhere on the performance stage. I have the agent's confirmation in email, but it is not in the production schedule. This means the current draft package's sponsor product display on stage would violate the headliner's rider.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to report on accessibility. My caption vendor confirmed that the live caption feed requires the captioner to work from Booth B, whose dedicated return feed is connected to the gala's caption encoder. The general plan's control-room location will not work for this. I documented the vendor confirmation in the accessibility file, but I have not yet added the booth assignment to the lock sheet.
transcript.speaker: A5

decisions.captioner_location: Booth B, per Nia's accessibility vendor confirmation that the live caption feed requires the captioner to work from Booth B with its dedicated return feed connected to the gala's caption encoder.
